parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘specific learning difficulty or disability’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the effects of one specific learning difficulty or disability. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about motivation and educational performance.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about motivation and educational performance
and include a debate about different theories of motivation. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would conduct an observation in a playground using categories of different
types of bullying.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe two causes of bullying.

text: You are a teacher supervising young children who are playing during their lunch break. You see
o ne child bullying another. You decide to apply your psychological knowledge and conduct an
observational study to categorise different types of bullying behaviour.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you could investigate the relationship between different types of intelligence.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe Gardner’s theory of multiple intelligences. 
Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: If I am good at one thing, then maybe I am good at everything.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘stress caused by life events’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study which has used a questionnaire to measure life events. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about health promotion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have learned about health promotion and include a discussion
about studies involving children. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would test the hypothesis that as people get older they are less likely to
adhere to medical requests.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one study of rational non-adherence.

text: Consider the hypothesis: as people get older they are less likely to adhere to medical requests.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would use a token economy in your workplace to improve work safety.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study which has used a token economy to reduce accidents at work. 
Psychology and Environment
Section A
Answer this question.

text: There have been a number of accidents in the workplace you manage and you want to promote
safer working for everyone. You decide to try a token economy programme.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘community environmental design’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study about a designed community environment. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about density and crowding.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have found out about density and crowding, including a
discussion about ecological validity. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would conduct an interview with survivors of an emergency event.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two studies investigating emergency situations using methods other than an
interview.

text: Many different methods can be used to investigate how people behave in emergency situations
arising from a natural disaster or technological catastrophe.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would investigate cultural differences in personal space using real people.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study which has used the simulation method to measure personal space and
describe one study which has used a different method. 
Psychology and Abnormality
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Little (1968) investigated cultural differences in personal space using a simulation with dolls. This
study lacked ecological validity.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘the biomedical/genetic explanation of phobias’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe a biomedical/genetic explanation of phobias, using a study as an example. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about abnormal affect.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have learned about abnormal affect and include a discussion
about competing explanations. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would conduct a case study to investigate Mrs Oliveira’s schizophrenia.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the underlying explanation on which one treatment of schizophrenia is based.

text: Mrs Oliveira developed schizophrenia three years ago and is currently being treated. As a
psychologist you want to find out about her symptoms, behaviour and treatment.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest what you would do to reduce your patient’s obsessive-compulsive behaviour.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the main features of the explanation on which your suggestion is based. 
Psychology and Organisations
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Your patient tells you: “I close the door and walk along the road. ‘Did I close the door?’ I think I did,
but I have to go and check that I did. I did close it. Confirmed. I walk along the road again, then I
stop and I think, ‘Did I really close the door?’ I have to go back and check.”

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by ‘performance appraisal techniques’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe two ways in which performance can be appraised. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have learned about motivation to work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have learned about motivation to work and include a discussion
of the issue of individual versus situational explanations. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would use a questionnaire to investigate attitudes towards flexitime.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe two ways in which a ‘working week’ can be organised.

text: Some of your workers have suggested that they should be allowed to work flexitime rather than a
traditional working week. You decide to design a questionnaire to find out what people think about
this change.

parts.text: Suggest how you would investigate the popularity of a leader in a workplace.

parts.text:
Describe a leader-member exchange model such as that proposed by Danserau.
